explanations: recordFailure does a read-modify-write: kv.get, add one, kv.set. Concurrent failures for the same username (exactly what a password-spraying script produces) read the same value and each write current + 1, so many attempts count as one and the lockout threshold is reached far later, or never. The store already offers incr, which increments atomically; it should be used (with expire on the first increment). As a side effect, each set also resets the window TTL.
LoginService calls recordSuccess after a successful verify, which deletes the fail key. Nothing waits for TTL, decrements, or sets it to the maximum.
failKey and lockKey call username.toLowerCase(), so both map to the same keys. There is no first-seen logic and the verifier does not affect key naming.

login() calls throttle.check first and returns { status: "locked", retryAfterSeconds } when the lock key is in the future, before verifier.verify runs. Correct passwords do not unlock, no failure is recorded, and the status is locked, not invalid.
